items.followUp: Differentiate between rotational motion and circular motion.

rubric.why: Shows the defining feature of translatory motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that all points of a body move the same distance in the same direction (or an equivalent definition).

rubric.why: Identifies the path that distinguishes linear motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the body moves along a straight line.

modelAnswer: In translatory motion, all points of a body move the same distance in the same direction.
In linear motion, a body moves along a straight line.

items.followUp: State two useful effects and two harmful effects of friction.

rubric.why: Gives two valid advantages of friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two valid advantages, such as helping us walk, write, or stop a vehicle using brakes.

rubric.why: Gives two valid disadvantages of friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two valid disadvantages, such as causing wear and tear, producing unwanted heat, or wasting energy.

modelAnswer: Advantages: Friction enables us to walk without slipping and allows brakes to stop vehicles.
Disadvantages: Friction causes wear and tear of moving parts and produces unwanted heat, wasting energy.

items.followUp: Define the centre of mass of a body.

rubric.why: Identifies the centre of gravity as a point in the body.
rubric.description: States that the centre of gravity is a point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a particular point in the body.

rubric.why: States the defining property of the centre of gravity.
rubric.description: States that the body's whole weight acts through that point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the entire weight of the body acts through the point.

modelAnswer: The centre of gravity of a body is the point through which the whole weight of the body acts.

items.followUp: A 20 cm spanner is used to apply a perpendicular force of 150 N to a nut. Find the torque.

rubric.why: Uses the torque relation and correct SI values.
rubric.description: Applies the torque formula with the spanner length converted to metres.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using torque = force × perpendicular distance and substituting 200 N and 0.15 m.

rubric.why: Gives the correct torque with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the answer 30 N m.

modelAnswer: Given: Force, F = 200 N; perpendicular distance, d = 15 cm = 0.15 m.
Substitution: τ = 200 N × 0.15 m = 30 N m.
Answer: The torque is 30 N m.

items.followUp: State the principle of moments for a body in equilibrium.

rubric.why: States the equality of turning effects on either side of the pivot.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that, for a body in equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments about a pivot equals the sum of anticlockwise moments.

modelAnswer: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of the clockwise moments about a pivot is equal to the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same pivot.

items.followUp: What energy conversion takes place in a solar cell?

rubric.why: Identifies the input energy and useful output of a solar cell.
rubric.description: Defines a solar cell by its energy conversion.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that a solar cell converts light energy (sunlight) directly into electrical energy.

modelAnswer: A solar cell is a device that converts light energy directly into electrical energy.

items.followUp: Define electrical power and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Defines electrical energy as the energy transferred or work done by an electric current.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that electrical energy is the work done by an electric current, or the energy transferred by it.

modelAnswer: Electrical energy is the work done by an electric current, or the energy transferred by the current.

items.followUp: State Pascal's law and name two devices that use it.

rubric.why: Includes the key idea that applied pressure is transmitted throughout an enclosed fluid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally in all directions.

rubric.why: Names two valid applications of Pascal's law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming any two applications, such as a hydraulic press, lift, jack, or brakes.

modelAnswer: Pascal's law states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally and undiminished in all directions throughout the fluid.
Applications include hydraulic presses and hydraulic brakes.
